title: Cambridge Analytica Harvests 87 Million Facebook Profiles for Trump Campaign
description_short: Cambridge Analytica Harvests 87 Million Facebook Profiles for Trump Campaign
description_medium: During the 2016 election, Cambridge Analytica — a data firm backed by Trump donor Robert Mercer and employing former Trump adviser Steve Bannon as a board member — harvested Facebook profiles of approximately 87 million users without consent through a third-party quiz app. The data was used to build psychographic profiles for targeted political advertising on behalf of the Trump campaign. Facebook did not publicly disclose the breach until 2018 after whistleblower Christopher Wylie went public.
description_long: During the 2016 election, Cambridge Analytica — a data firm backed by Trump donor Robert Mercer and employing former Trump adviser Steve Bannon as a board member — harvested Facebook profiles of approximately 87 million users without consent through a third-party quiz app. The data was used to build psychographic profiles for targeted political advertising on behalf of the Trump campaign. Facebook did not publicly disclose the breach until 2018 after whistleblower Christopher Wylie went public. Facebook was fined $5 billion by the FTC in 2019, and Cambridge Analytica dissolved amid the scandal. The controversy joined data collection to political profiling: personal information obtained through an app could be used beyond the expectations of people whose profiles were included. The figure for potentially affected users is not a count of people persuaded to vote for Trump. title: Trump Guts Endangered Species Act Protections
description_short: Trump Guts Endangered Species Act Protections
description_medium: In 2019, the Trump administration finalized sweeping changes to the Endangered Species Act, weakening protections that had helped recover species like bald eagles, grizzly bears, and humpback whales from the brink of extinction for nearly 50 years. The new rules made it easier to remove species from the endangered list, allowed economic factors to be weighed against habitat protection, and weakened protections for threatened species.
description_long: In 2019, the Trump administration finalized sweeping changes to the Endangered Species Act, weakening protections that had helped recover species like bald eagles, grizzly bears, and humpback whales from the brink of extinction for nearly 50 years. The new rules made it easier to remove species from the endangered list, allowed economic factors to be weighed against habitat protection, and weakened protections for threatened species. Conservation biologists called the changes the most significant weakening of the Endangered Species Act since its passage in 1973, warning it would accelerate species loss as climate change intensified. The rules affected how protections were applied, rather than repealing the Endangered Species Act itself. Changes involving threatened species, habitat decisions, and removal from the list can alter the practical scope of conservation even while the statute remains in force. The biologists' warnings described expected risks to species recovery and should remain predictions, rather than proof of particular extinctions caused by the rules.

title: Trump Shares Classified Location of US Nuclear Submarines to Philippines' Duterte
description_short: Trump Shares Classified Location of US Nuclear Submarines to Philippines' Duterte
description_medium: According to a 2017 transcript of a phone call leaked to The Intercept, President Trump disclosed to Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte the location of two US nuclear submarines in the waters near the Korean Peninsula, information considered highly classified. The disclosure was made casually, apparently as a boast during a congratulatory call, without any evident national security rationale. Former intelligence officials described the disclosure as a potentially serious breach of operational security.
description_long: According to a 2017 transcript of a phone call leaked to The Intercept, President Trump disclosed to Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte the location of two US nuclear submarines in the waters near the Korean Peninsula, information considered highly classified. The disclosure was made casually, apparently as a boast during a congratulatory call, without any evident national security rationale. Former intelligence officials described the disclosure as a potentially serious breach of operational security. Duterte, known for his extra-judicial killings and human rights abuses, was considered an unreliable confidant for such sensitive military information. The transcript and officials' assessments are different kinds of evidence. Trump's relationship with Duterte gives the conversation political context, while the entry does not infer an additional agreement or military consequence from the disclosure alone.

title: Attorney General Merrick Garland Appoints Jack Smith as Special Counsel for Trump Criminal Investigations
description_short: Attorney General Merrick Garland Appoints Jack Smith as Special Counsel for Trump Criminal Investigations
description_medium: On November 18, 2022, Attorney General Merrick Garland announced the appointment of former chief prosecutor for the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, Jack Smith, as Special Counsel. Smith was tasked with overseeing two ongoing federal criminal investigations into Donald Trump: the mishandling of classified documents found at Mar-a-Lago and attempts to interfere with the lawful transfer of power following the 2020 presidential election. Garland cited Trump's formal announcement of his 2024 presidential campaign three days prior, alongside President Joe Biden's stated intention to run, as making the appointment in the public interest.
description_long: On November 18, 2022, Attorney General Merrick Garland announced the appointment of former chief prosecutor for the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, Jack Smith, as Special Counsel. Smith was tasked with overseeing two ongoing federal criminal investigations into Donald Trump: the mishandling of classified documents found at Mar-a-Lago and attempts to interfere with the lawful transfer of power following the 2020 presidential election. Garland cited Trump's formal announcement of his 2024 presidential campaign three days prior, alongside President Joe Biden's stated intention to run, as making the appointment in the public interest. Smith pledged to conduct the investigations independently, urgently, and strictly according to the law. The appointment transferred responsibility for specified investigations, rather than announcing criminal charges or resolving whether Trump had committed an offense. Garland's stated reason focused on the political circumstances created by prospective presidential candidates. Smith's commitment described how he intended to conduct the work. The two investigative subjects remained distinct: retention of classified material and actions affecting the transfer of presidential power. The entry records the creation of the special-counsel role and its mandate, without importing later prosecutions into the announcement.
